newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn protests to Burma over refusing visa.
newsitem.headline: Bonn protests to Burma over refusing visa.

text.p: Germany protested to Burma on Thursday over its decision to refuse entry to a former German cabinet minister who heads a foundation which speaks out on human rights, the Foreign Ministry said.

Otto Lambsdorff, a former economics minister and leading member of the liberal Free Democratic Party (FDP), had planned to visit the country to hold talks with both the Burmese leadership and democracy movement leader Aung San Suu Kyi.
Lambsdorff said on Wednesday his visa application had been refused by the Burmese embassy in Bonn.

A ministry spokesman told Reuters that Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel had called on the Burmese government to rethink the decision and had said it was inacceptable to stop such a renowned politician from entering Burma.
The ministry said German officials would meet the Burmese ambassador in Bonn and that the German ambassador in Rangoon would lodge an official complaint with the Burmese government.

Lambsdorff is chairman of the Friedrich Naumann Institute, which is closely linked to the FDP. He said the decision showed that the Burmese military regime was not interested in political dialogue with Nobel laureate Aung San Suu Kyi.
The institute said the Burmese embassy had declined Lambsdorff's visa application because it considered his visit to be "inappropriate for political reasons".
Lambsdorff sent an open letter to Kinkel on Wednesday asking him to press for the European Union to adopt a clear line on Burma.
In particular, he said a meeting of EU ministers later this month should strip the Southeast Asian nation of preferential trade status as a punishment for massive use of slave labour.
Last year the Naumann foundation sparked a brief diplomatic row with China after it invited Tibet's spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama, to speak at a conference partly financed with government money.
